note: Release-body entries that BOTH surfaces must judge the same way. Read by `the_two_surfaces_agree_on_every_shared_release_body_fixture` in crates/dux-core/src/release_notes.rs and by releaseNotes.test.ts in crates/dux-web/web. `renderable` is what `entry_is_renderable` / `entryIsRenderable` must answer. The four cases marked `divergence` were measured disagreeing before the matchers were built from the shared invisible set and given the same single left-to-right pass: one surface showed the notes and the other the no-notes explanation for the same release.

cases.what: an HTML break split by a next-line character
cases.divergence: Rust's char::is_whitespace covers U+0085 and JavaScript's \s does not, so this was empty in the terminal and renderable in the browser

cases.what: an HTML break split by a byte-order mark
cases.divergence: JavaScript's \s covers U+FEFF and Rust's char::is_whitespace does not, so this was empty in the browser and renderable in the terminal

cases.what: a self-closed HTML break split by a byte-order mark
cases.divergence: same U+FEFF split, on the self-closing spelling

cases.what: an HTML break interrupted by a comment
cases.divergence:
the web ran comments, breaks and invisibles as three sequential passes, so removing the comment first MANUFACTURED a break out of text that never held one; one left-to-right pass on both sides leaves the visible `
` text instead

cases.what: an HTML break spaced with an ordinary space
the rule the release pipeline appends

cases.entry: A note <!-- aside --> that still reads.

cases.what: a lone dash, which is not a thematic break
text that merely starts like a break
